1. Proceedings in the present case arises from filing of DAR in FIR No.33/17 of PS Vivek Vihar under Section 279/337 IPC regarding receiving of grievous injuries to petitioner Vinod Kumar in the road side accident.
The accident in question took place on 21.01.2017 at about 08:15 a.m.
As per petitioner/ complainant on 21.01.2017 at 08:15 a.m. he was going from Seemapuri Border to Baldev Park on Gramin Seva No. DL-2W- 3439 of white colour along with other 15-16 co-passengers.

When the said vehicle was descending Vivek Vihar flyover, suddenly driver of the vehicle had increased the speed of the MACT No.294/2017 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 1 MALIK Date:
2024.02.13 16:14:42 +0530 vehicle and driving the vehicle rashly and negligently at a very high speed.
Driver of the said vehicle was warned by the petitioner and other co-passengers to reduce the speed but he continued doing so.

When said vehicle reached in front of Petrol Pump Vivek Vihar,
driver of the said vehicle climbed it on the divider and hit it against sign board on road due to which petitioner as well as co-passengers received injuries.
Someone informed the police at 100 no. and driver of the said vehicle fled away from the spot.
Police came at the spot and removed the petitioner to Dr. Hedgewar hospital.
It is stated that the offending vehicle was owned by respondent no. 2 and it was insured with respondent no. 3/ Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company.
2. Notice of the DAR was issued to the respondents.

Respondent no. 1 and 2 appeared in the court Dar - Vinod Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74937428/

sentences.text: In order to prove the manner in which accident has taken place, petitioner/injured (PW6) in his affidavit of examination in chief has testified that on 21.10.2017 at about 8.15 a.m. he was going towards fire station Vivek Vihar from his work as he was working as fire operator by Gramin Sewa bearing no.DL-2W-3439 from Seemapuri Border.
PW1 states that he was sitting in said vehicle along with 3 other co-passengers and thereafter driver of said vehicle started driving it.
When said vehicle started descending Vivek Vihar flyover, sudden driver of the said vehicle increased the speed of vehicle , driving it rashly and negligently in a zig zag manner.

Petitioner stated to have warned the driver/respondent no.1 of said vehicle to drive the vehicle slowly and when said vehicle reached near road no.56, in front of petrol pump, Vivek Vihar, driver lost control upon vehicle and after hitting the divider again hit into a signboard.
Due to said impact petitioner/injured suffered serious and grievous injuries and he was taken to Dr. Hedgewar Hospital.

12. Having considered the evidence, this Tribunal finds that evidence of PW6 is cogent and specific with regard to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 in driving of offending vehicle no.
DL-2W-3439.
Moreover FIR No.33/2017 was registered in which respondent no.1 was charge sheeted in criminal case.
Moreover DAR Ex.PW6/1 also indicate that it is respondent no.1 who was responsible in causing of accident.
Documents annexed with DAR shows that site plan of the place of accident and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle is on record.
Thus, testimony of petitioner/PW6 coupled with material available on record clearly establish that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
Thus, this Tribunal concludes that petitioner has proved that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1. in driving of offending vehicle no. DL-2W-3439.
Accordingly issue stands decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

sentences.text: "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas MACT No.294/2017 Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.02.13 16:15:47 +0530 non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock,
pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future;
(ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience,
discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK MACT No.294/2017 Page 6 Date: 2024.02.13 16:16:07 +0530 the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

Dar - Vinod Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74937428/
4 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
 (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage)
 (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of Digitally signed by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.294/2017 MALIK Date:
2024.02.13 Page 7 16:16:16 +0530 the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-

Loss of future earning due to disability :
19.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

sentences.text: If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
MACT No.294/2017 2024.02.13  16:16:43 +0530 Page 10 any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."

....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.

13. We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.

7
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases,
where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).
(iii).
The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession, occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
20. Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the present case it is evident on record that as a result of the injuries sustained by petitioner in an accident, he suffered 21% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb.

In this regard PW1 Dr. Binod Kalita, Specialist, Orthopedic from Jag Pravesh Chandra, Hospital, Delhi, produced the record relating to disability certificate no.148/DBN/2021/1099 dated 15.02.2021, issued to injured Vinod Kumar which is Ex.PW1/A.

The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.
As per case of petitioner, he was working as Fire Operator in Fire station Vivek Vihar, Delhi on contract basis.
21. It is argued by the counsel for the petitioner that due to accidental injuries and permanent disability, petitioner lost his job of being Fire Operator.
PW1 stated in cross-examination that he cannot comment upon functional disability of the petitioner however he would face difficulties in lifting heavy weight.
22. In Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) Hon'ble Apex Court in para 11 and 12 has observed that Tribunal should not be a silent spectator when medical evidence is tendered regarding injuries.

Tribunal is required to hold inquiry into the SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK MACT No.294/2017 Page 12 Date: 2024.02.13 16:17:01 +0530 claim for determining just compensation by assessing the medical permanent disability as well as functional disability keeping in view nature of work,
profession etc. of the injured.
The percentage of permanent disability of whole body cannot be presumed to be percentage loss of earning.
Therefore Tribunal is bound to assess corresponding functional disability to compute the future loss of income.
23. Having considered the entire evidence, medical documents reflect that petitioner suffered grievous injuries and suffered 21% of permanent disability.

In such circumstances when petitioner Dar - Vinod Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74937428/
8 has lost his job of being Fire Operator on account of his accidental injuries, this tribunal is of considered view that the functional disability of the petitioner in relation to his job was double of the medical disability i.e. 21% of medical permanent disability.

Pain & Sufferings:

"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.

(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of pleadings as come on the record following issues were framed on 20.02.2018:
(1) Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.294/2017 MALIK Date:
2024.02.13 Page 2 16:15:04 +0530 vehicle No. DL-2W-3439 on 21.01.2017 at 08:30 am, at Road No. 56, infront of Petrol Pump, Vivek Vihar, Delhi in rash and rash and negligent manner and caused injuries to the petitioner?
OPP (2)Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extend and from whom?
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
(i) Whether the disablement is  permanent or temporary;
 (ii) If the disablement is permanent,
whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body, that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
MACT No.294/2017 2024.02.13  16:16:43 +0530 Page 10 any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are MACT No.294/2017 Page 3
SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
Dar - Vinod Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74937428/
2 2024.02.13 16:15:14 +0530 not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
(MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012),
Thus, testimony of petitioner/PW6 coupled with material available on record clearly establish that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of Digitally signed by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.294/2017 MALIK Date:
2024.02.13 Page 7 16:16:16 +0530 the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
13. We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
Dar - Vinod Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74937428/
7
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.
The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.
The percentage of permanent disability of whole body cannot be presumed to be percentage loss of earning.
Therefore Tribunal is bound to assess corresponding functional disability to compute the future loss of income.
23. Having considered the entire evidence, medical documents reflect that petitioner suffered grievous injuries and suffered 21% of permanent disability.
In such circumstances when petitioner Dar - Vinod Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74937428/
8 has lost his job of being Fire Operator on account of his accidental injuries, this tribunal is of considered view that the functional disability of the petitioner in relation to his job was double of the medical disability i.e. 21% of medical permanent disability.
For assessing the future prospects,
petitioner would considered to be suffering from functional disability to the extent of 42%.
24. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also
[refer:
Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].
As per photocopy of Aadhar card and PAN Card Ex.PW6/3, date of birth of petitioner is 01.01.1975.
As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 14 as applicable to age group between 41-45 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Thus, considering that the petitioner was not having any permanent job and below the age of 50 years at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 25% towards future prospects has to be counted.
Keeping in view the medical documents placed on record, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner must have engaged the services of some attendant and he is required to be awarded compensation under this head for a period of four months.
Therefore petitioner in the opinion of this Tribunal is also entitled for minimum wages of unskilled worker i.e. Rs.9724/- X 4 which comes out to be Rs.
38,896/-.
Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.50,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
